feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector leadership: clear positioning, relevant scope, and good evidence of progression and ownership. It reads professionally, but it is slightly repetitive, a bit dense, and could sharpen impact by adding more outcomes and trimming overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior narrative: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support the “digital platform and communications systems leader” positioning.  
- Good credibility signals: named platforms, scale metrics, governance scope, and concrete projects make the experience believable and substantive.  
- Writing is polished overall: tone is consistent, action-oriented, and largely free of grammar or spelling errors.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Add stronger results language: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (engagement lifts, efficiency gains, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma, and punctuation/hyphenation style varies slightly across sections. No major misspellings found; grammar is strong overall.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading” or “driving” enterprise digital platforms, governance, and content operations.
- Add one concrete proof point from recent experience, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related areas: web modernization, analytics, editorial governance, and multimedia/AI experiences.
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Built and scaled digital ecosystems including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled content discovery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” repeats the subtitle’s leadership positioning.
- The long list of capabilities overlaps with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but this section overlaps heavily with the summary and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize differentiators and reduce generic phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use sharper, outcome-oriented wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “website modernization,” and “Digital governance, editorial workflows & publishing systems” for specificity.
- Group related items and trim repetition with other sections. Suggested version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance, editorial workflows & publishing systems • Analytics, dashboards & reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search & content discovery • Workflow automation & platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production, livestreaming & studio operations
- Standardize style: use either “and” or “&” consistently; “public-sector” should stay hyphenated.
- Consider replacing “content experiences” with “content discovery” or “user experiences” for clearer meaning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills categories.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also repeated in Work Experience and Technical + IT.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening phrasing and adding a clearer “selected projects” framing would improve impact and reduce redundancy.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Retitle as “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, outcome-oriented line.
- Standardize style: use parallel action verbs and consistent punctuation; spell out “10 x 20-foot” for style consistency.
- Add specificity where possible: audience, scale, platform, or business purpose (for example, legislative content discovery, campaign growth, conference engagement).
- Consider this tighter version: AI Hybrid Search — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level chat to improve policy-content discovery. We Are Counties Microsite — Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling, downloadable resources, and a modular architecture for future expansion.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most additive item here because it introduces the interactive display and cross-channel campaign format.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around strategic ownership, technical depth, and 1–2 concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client type: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate bullets to 4–5 and use stronger verbs: “Built enterprise workflows, analytics, and governance models to improve cross-channel communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Combine Drupal/CMS points: “Designed and implemented Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, downloadable toolkits, and front-end/CMS enhancements for high-traffic public sites.”
- Keep the AI work as the differentiator and add metrics if possible: “Spearheaded AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.” Add launch status, adoption, or efficiency gains if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats NACo Director of Digital Media; emphasize consulting ownership or client-specific transformation.
- Microsites/AI search duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer hold examples.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It can be sharper by foregrounding the biggest outcomes, tightening channel-management language, and avoiding overlap with earlier NACo roles on newsletters/video operations.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullets into one stronger achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused; add metrics if available: email growth/open rates, social engagement, video output, event reach, cost savings from in-house production.
- Tighten the final bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting; established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry at the strategic/enterprise level.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo bullets; emphasize studio buildout and organizational capability instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about operational leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite opening to sharpen scope and seniority: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial planning and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent publishing workflows and improved coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” closely repeat the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- Weekly video updates also overlap with the 2015–2018 role; keep this version focused on scaling/owning the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership themes not already covered elsewhere, especially governance, enterprise strategy, and audience outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, senior-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy content strategy
- Audience-centered content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “content strategy” to better match the CV’s systems/operations focus.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g. “Audience-centered content planning and discovery” to echo the AI search / usability work.
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid mixing leadership, channels, and tactics in uneven phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use a distinct angle such as “content strategy” or “stakeholder communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section and reads as a tool dump rather than a senior, impact-oriented topline summary. Refocus this item on current platforms and execution strengths most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the long list with grouped, higher-level phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop or de-emphasize older/lower-signal items here: remove jQuery unless it is still actively used in current work.
- Consider prioritizing recent evidence: put “Drupal,” “CMS modernization,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” first, since they align with 2022–present work.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-linked: “CMS modernization for large public-sector sites” to echo the 10,000+ page migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating it verbatim in both places if possible.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” As a topline skills item, it should emphasize strategic analytics leadership and outcomes, not just repeat platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity
- KPI framework design and executive reporting
- SEO, user behavior analysis, and performance optimization
- Put the highest-value concepts first: analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting.
- Tighten wording: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards.”
- If space allows elsewhere, quantify impact in experience bullets instead of here (e.g. reporting for 10,000+ page site / 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.
- It also overlaps with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep this section more strategic and that one more tool-specific.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it more senior, outcomes-oriented, and tied to recent leadership-level multimedia work rather than listing production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event operations
- In-house studio buildout and PTZ camera workflows
- Multimedia systems supporting advocacy and executive communications
- If space allows, add one signal of scale or ownership, e.g. “Built and operated an in-house broadcast studio” or “Supported recurring advocacy programming and live events.”
- Keep wording consistent with leadership tone used elsewhere; avoid overly tactical phrasing like “video editing” unless paired with strategy/operations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one instance.
- “PTZ camera systems” is quite tactical for this senior CV unless supported by a studio/operations framing.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this item to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeating names only.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/recency: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages, with Drupal first and qualified.
- Consider replacing the weakest/least relevant platform with a stronger descriptor, e.g. “Drupal CMS modernization” or “Enterprise CMS administration.”
- Keep platform names only if other technical items already carry implementation detail; otherwise add one parenthetical for your lead platform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by Topline Skills > “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the seniority of the CV unless it supports a specific recent project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and tools most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If space allows, add light proficiency framing: Front-end development and web implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery; API integrations; deployment/automation with GitHub Actions; edge scripting with Cloudflare Workers; tag management with Google Tag Manager
- If you can substantiate from recent projects, add one outcome-oriented qualifier elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “used for microsite builds, workflow automation, and analytics implementation” rather than here

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Consider removing either this item or the overlapping Topline Skills line to avoid repetitive skills stacking.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as an undifferentiated software list. Since workflow automation is already emphasized elsewhere, this item should be tighter and grouped to show systems thinking rather than repeat generic collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, e.g.: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello”
- Move general collaboration tools out unless they were admin/implementation platforms you directly managed; Slack, Teams, and Basecamp add less value here.
- If accurate, add a qualifier to show depth: “built automations,” “managed workflow systems,” or “designed cross-team processes in Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier.”
- Consider a cleaner final version: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello” or “Airtable systems • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana/Trello workflow management”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Slack/Teams overlap with standard workplace familiarity rather than distinctive technical capability.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale of your email leadership. It should signal enterprise-level platform ownership, especially given your recent NACo and consulting work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, member communications)**
- If accurate, strengthen further with scope: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • enterprise newsletter distribution • audience segmentation • campaign automation**
- Keep only platforms you’ve directly used in recent roles; lead with the most current/strategic system.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations”; keep this item tool-focused, not functional.
- Email leadership already appears in multiple NACo roles, so avoid adding generic phrases like “email strategy” unless tied to platform capability.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it to emphasize analysis/optimization capabilities rather than repeating platforms already evidenced in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Data & Optimization Tools
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation
- Replace “A/B testing” with “Experimentation” unless you’ve directly run formal tests; it’s broader and safer.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards” to sound more outcome-oriented and senior.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider keeping the detailed list here and shortening the Topline entry to higher-level capabilities only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in your 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating all five elsewhere unless needed for ATS.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup rather than achievement. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and content output, with metrics if you can add them.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize advancement and scope: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support operations across web, email, social, and video.”
- Make contributions more concrete: replace “major website refresh” with the platform/CMS, size, or outcome if known.
- Clarify output and leadership: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of videos/livestreams, audience reach, traffic/email impact, or team size.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this entry as the launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles at NACo.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize initiative and scope: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer action such as “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes launched, audiences reached, internal teams supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item focused on research/program support plus the first podcast.
- Avoid repeating broad web/email/social responsibilities that are better covered in more recent roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skills, but this item is a bit mixed and overlaps with the stronger “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” section. Tighten it to emphasize software/tools rather than production capabilities already shown elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia & Creative Software
- Rewrite as: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want to keep one workflow item, use: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast editing
